<reason>CON made the motion easier to decide: large fraud and access wins only arrive with the near-universal use that is itself the spine and honeypot. PRO never escaped SSN-style function creep except with hope that law plus design would succeed where convenience already won, while CON’s identity-vs-credit-card distinction undercut PRO’s best “ubiquity is not centralization” reply.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>CON Rebuttal 2: three cryptographic yes-or-no checks still map a life, and a token that authorizes who you are everywhere is not a credit card—directly damaging PRO’s concentration and design-containment claims.</best_rebuttal>
